cards.text: Some time later, Ben-hadad, king of Aram, gathers his entire army. He marches up and besieges Samaria, a city in Israel. Friend, buckle up.

cards.question: Aram's army stays camped around Samaria for a long, long time. What hits the city?

cards.text: It gets so bad that a donkey's head sells for eighty shekels of silver. Friend, the expired coupon I shared a junk drawer with still believed in itself, and even IT never thought it was worth THAT much!

cards.question: True or false: during the siege of Samaria, even dove's dung sells for silver.

cards.text: The king of Israel is passing by on the city wall when a woman cries out to him, "Help me, my lord the king!"

cards.question: True or false: the king of Israel tells the woman that if the LORD doesn't help her, he has no way to help her either.

cards.text: The king asks what's wrong, and she tells him another woman said they would eat her son first and the other woman's son tomorrow. So they boiled her son and ate him, but the next day the other woman had hidden her own son.

cards.question: When the king of Israel hears the woman's words, what does he do?

answers.text: He sends for the other woman

cards.text: As he passes by on the wall, the people see sackcloth under his clothes, right next to his skin. Then he swears that God may punish him, and severely, if the head of Elisha son of Shaphat, the prophet, stays on his shoulders through this day.
Elisha is sitting in his house with the elders. Before the king's messenger even gets there, Elisha tells them this murderer has sent someone to cut off his head.

cards.question: When the king's messenger arrives at the house, what does Elisha tell the elders to do?

answers.text: Shut the door to keep him out
Open the door and welcome him
Send him back with an answer

cards.question: True or false: Elisha says the king's own footsteps are right behind the messenger.

cards.text: While Elisha is still speaking with the elders, the messenger comes down to him. Then the king says, "This calamity is from the LORD."

cards.question: True or false: the king of Israel says the calamity in Samaria is from the LORD, so he'll keep waiting on the LORD.

cards.text: Elisha answers with the word of the LORD: about this time tomorrow at the gate of Samaria, a seah of fine flour will sell for a shekel, and two seahs of barley will sell for a shekel.

cards.question: During the siege, a donkey's head sold for eighty shekels of silver. What does Elisha's message about the flour and barley mean?

answers.text: Food will be cheap and plentiful
Only the king's household will eat

cards.text: The officer whose arm the king leans on answers, "Look, even if the LORD were to make windows in heaven, could this really happen?" Friend, that's not just a no, that's a no with SPECIAL EFFECTS.

cards.question: Elisha tells the officer who doubts the word of the LORD that he'll see it with his own eyes but won't ___ any of it.

cards.text: Now four men with leprosy are at the entrance of the city gate, asking one another, "Why just sit here until we die?" Friend, I sat in the back of a junk drawer for YEARS asking that exact question.

cards.question: The four men with leprosy work it out. If they go into the city, they'll die from the famine, and if they sit at the gate, they'll die anyway. Where do they decide to go?

answers.text: Over to the camp of the Arameans
Down to the land of Egypt

cards.text: Their plan: "If they let us live, we will live; if they kill us, we will die." Friend, when the best thing on the table is a MAYBE, you take the maybe!
So at twilight they get up and head for the camp of the Arameans. They reach the outskirts of the camp and take a look.

cards.question: True or false: at the edge of the Aramean camp, the four men find soldiers asleep in their tents.

cards.text: Not a man to be found. Here's why: the Lord had caused the Arameans to hear something.

cards.question: What does the Lord cause the Arameans to hear?

answers.text: Chariots and horses and a great army
The walls of Samaria cracking apart
Trumpets blowing from the city gate

cards.text: The Arameans tell each other the king of Israel must have hired the kings of the Hittites and Egyptians, so at twilight they run for their lives. A whole army, chased off by a SOUND, friend.

cards.question: The Arameans run for their lives and leave their whole camp ___ behind them.

cards.text: The Arameans left behind their tents, horses and donkeys. The four men walk into a tent to eat and drink, then carry off silver, gold and clothing and go hide it.

cards.question: True or false: after hiding their first load, the four men go into another tent and carry off more.
Finally, with their loot hidden, the four men stop and talk. What do they say to each other?

answers.text: We are not doing what is right
We should take it all before dawn
We should leave before they return

cards.text: They know it's a day of good news, and if they keep quiet until morning, their sin will overtake them. Friend, that's finding a box of cookies in the break room and telling NOBODY, and that ALWAYS catches up with you.

cards.question: The four men decide not to keep the good news to themselves. Who do they decide to tell?

cards.text: So the four men call out to the gatekeepers of Samaria: nobody's in the Aramean camp, just tethered horses and donkeys, and the tents are still standing. The gatekeepers shout the news, and it reaches the king's household.

cards.question: The king of Israel gets up in the night and talks to his servants. What does he say the Arameans have done?

answers.text: Left camp to hide and ambush them
Gone home to bring more soldiers
Left the camp as a peace offering

cards.text: A whole camp sitting empty, and the king's first word is TRAP. Then one of his servants suggests sending scouts out with five of the horses still left in the city.

cards.question: Why does the king's servant say it's worth risking five of the horses?

answers.text: Everyone left in the city is doomed anyway
The horses are too weak to carry riders
The Arameans never attack in the dark

cards.text: So the scouts take two chariots with horses, and the king sends them after the Aramean army. His orders: "Go and see."

cards.question: True or false: the scouts find the road clean, with no sign the Arameans came through.

cards.text: The whole way to the Jordan is littered with clothing and equipment the Arameans threw off in a hurry. The scouts come back and tell the king.

cards.question: True or false: once the scouts report back, the people of Samaria go out and plunder the Aramean camp.
Once the people plunder the Aramean camp, what happens to the price of flour and barley in Samaria?

answers.text: It drops just as Elisha said
It stays as high as before
It doubles by the next morning

cards.text: Now the king had put the officer whose arm he leaned on in charge of the gate. Yes, friend, the man who asked about windows in heaven.

cards.question: The people pour through the gateway where the king's officer is in charge. What happens to him?

answers.text: The people trample him and he dies
He eats the first flour from the camp
He chases the Arameans to the Jordan

cards.text: It happened just as the man of God told the king about the flour and the barley, and just as he told the officer. Every word of it came true, friend.
